title: A correlation cap of 0.5 selects one input in optimal positive readouts of 69 of 130 selected Allen input groups
abstract: We tested positive linear readouts of linked Allen cortical input groups when cross-input noise correlation is unknown. Means were assigned from first-pulse medians. Standard deviations were taken from released response summaries. For any positive readout and a uniform absolute correlation cap r, the adverse covariance has all off-diagonal correlations equal to r. The ideal readout uses one input exactly when r reaches the ratio of the second largest to largest individual signal-to-noise ratio. At cap 0.5, 69 of 130 selected groups use one input: 15 of 29 mouse excitatory, 48 of 89 mouse inhibitory, and 6 of 12 human excitatory groups. Weights chosen for independent noise lose the best-input guarantee in 96 groups at this cap. An assumed factor 1.10 error box certifies 46 single-input solutions. Exhaustive subset and numerical checks agree. Unknown covariance, median-to-mean error, recording noise, selected slice groups and small high-count samples prevent a biological input-selection claim. Original code, a proof, aggregate results and retrieval steps support reproduction. External records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Conditional model results. Correlation caps are assumptions. A shows the exact threshold distribution. B shows the fraction of groups with one active input. C shows median optimal worst-case squared SNR gain over the best input.

citations.reason: Uses its published sample definition and model motivation. New code; no code or record tables reused.
